To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CD45 tyrosin phosphatase is essential for the TCR-mediated signals induced by Campat-1H.
the Campath-1 H antibody induces protein tyrosine phosphotyrosine signals in T cells by a CD45-dependent mechanism, but does not induce the calcium signals associated with T cell activation.
Campath- 1H, a therapeutic antibody, activates T cells via the TCR in a CD45-dependent manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of molecular mechanisms involved in the activation of T cells by the humanized monoclonal antibody Campath-1 H, and the identification of the molecular basis for the lymphocyte-depleting effects of Campath 1 H in vivo.
the molecular basis for Campath-1-mediated T cell activation and the mechanisms by which the Campath-1 mAb induces lymphocyte depletion in humans.
understanding the mechanism of action of Campath- 1H and the molecular basis of its immunosuppressive activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Campath-1 H antibody is not an agonistic anti-CD3 antibody.
CD45 is a critical regulator of the TCR-dependent signalling events induced by Campath1H.
CD52 is a T cell receptor-associated molecule that is capable of inducing T cell activation, and that Campath- 1H, the CD52-specific mAb used in the clinic, is a T cell activating agent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD52 mAb ligation of the TCR induces signals via CD45 and that this is the basis of the lymphocyte depletion induced by Campath1H.
Campath- 1H, by binding to CD52, is capable of inducing a TCR-dependent signaling pathway in primary T cells.
the CD45 phosphatase regulates the CD3-mediated signal transduction in T cells by modulating the activity of the T-cell receptor associated tyrosine kinseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TCR can signal in the absence of a co-stimulatory signal.
the TCR is a highly versatile receptor, which can be activated in a variety of ways.
CD52 is an activating antigen for T cells.
